articles.title: Apple's new desktop computers are designed specifically for local AI development
articles.summary: Apple has announced new iterations of the Mac mini and Mac Studio along with the M6, the first 2nm chip in Apple's M-series lineup, and the M5 Ultra, Apple's most powerful chip. There aren't any major new features for either machine. The devices have been recently popular for local AI inference and software development due to their unified memory architecture and fast CPUs and GPUs on their systems-on-a-chip. The Mac mini with M6 starts at $899 with 16GB of memory, and the Mac Studio with the M5 Max starts at $2,499.

articles.title: OpenAI Claims Its New Chips Can Outperform Nvidia Processors in Tests
articles.summary: OpenAI's new 'Jalapeno' chips performed better than Nvidia's current lineup during testing. The company plans to use the new chips to support its AI models later this year. The chip should significantly reduce costs for OpenAI as it rolls out more widely. OpenAI created the chip in a partnership with Broadcom.

articles.title: Amazon eyes ‘fully automated' delivery stations to bring robotics to the last mile
articles.summary: Amazon's fulfillment centers are equipped with the latest robots and automation, but its delivery stations still remain mostly manual. The company is now developing an internal project to build fully automated delivery stations. The technology behind Project Tetromino could come from Boxbot, a robotics startup that uses conveyors and AI-driven storage trays to automatically sequence packages for vehicle loading. Amazon has opened up a Last Mile Innovation Center in Germany to test delivery station technologies.

articles.title: SpaceX to Spend $100 Billion on New Spaceport in Louisiana
articles.summary: SpaceX is committing $100 billion to build a launch facility in southern Louisiana as part of its plans to send multiple rockets into space every day. The new facility, named Starbase Louisiana, will be located on 125,000 acres of coastal marshland and bring 3,000 jobs to the area. SpaceX will need at least several locales to fulfill its goal of sending thousands of rockets into orbit a year. The company is constantly exploring viable sites to expand its operations, domestically and internationally.

articles.title: Knowledge Compressor
articles.summary: Natural language tends to contain quite a bit of repetition and redundancy, which isn't inherently bad, but it comes with tradeoffs. With AI, repetition can cost a significant amount of tokens when working with substantial knowledge content. This study looks at whether documentation can be made less repetitive through compression. It found that typical technical documentation can have its token count cut in half without substantially reducing its usefulness to language models.

articles.title: Introducing Run SDK: secure eval for your agents
articles.summary: Run SDK is a package from Vercel for executing untrusted JavaScript or TypeScript without giving it direct access to apps or systems. It evaluates JavaScript or type-stripped TypeScript in a fresh QuickJS context inside a worker thread and exposes selected operations through hostFunctions. Calls cross the sandbox boundary through serialization. A host function may return a promise, so existing service clients can sit behind this interface without being passed into the sandbox.

articles.title: Apple Holds Farewell Party for Tim Cook as Ternus Prepares to Take Over
articles.summary: Tim Cook will step down as Apple's CEO on September 1. The company held a celebration for Cook on August 23, a day before his 15th anniversary as Apple CEO. Approximately 200 people attended the party, where the band OneRepublic performed. Cook will remain with Apple and become the company's executive chairman. John Ternus, who has been at Apple since 2001, will take over as CEO.

articles.title: Could Nvidia Default?
articles.summary: Credit Default Swaps insuring against an Nvidia debt default have doubled in price in the last two months. The company gave a $105 billion residual value guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center earlier this month, and it has also been involved in two other $500 billion deals this month. It has been reported to have been involved in over 300 financing deals in the last five years. Analysts are worried an AI downturn could see the circular deals entered into by Nvidia with other AI players unravel, which could result in cascading losses.
